11         QUALIFICATIONS.

12   A.    I hold a bachelor's in business administration with a double major in Economics

13         and Finance from The University of Texas at El Paso and a Master of Arts in

14         Economics with a concentration in Public Utility Policy & Regulation from New

15         Mexico State University ("NMSU").

18         In November 2014, I earned a progressive promotion to Staff Financial Analyst and

19         in October of 2016 was promoted to Senior Rate Analyst. Finally, I was promoted

20         to my current position as a Supervisor - Rates and Regulatory, in September 2020.

 1   Q12. WHAT TYPE OF ADJUSTMENTS HAVE BEEN MADE TO EPE’S BASE

 2        PERIOD DATA TO DETERMINE HISTORICAL TEST YEAR PERIOD

 3        BASE REVENUES?

 4   A.   In order to ensure that the test year is indicative of what is likely to occur under

 5        normal, recurring operating conditions, EPE has annualized and normalized Base

 6        Period billing and usage data to determine Historical Test Year Period base

 7        revenues at present rates. These adjustments, tabulated in Exhibit RFG-1, are

 8        explained below and primarily enumerate the impact of (1) annualizing test year-

 9        end customer growth or decline; (2) billing determinants that have been adjusted to

10        reflect normal weather; (3) annualizing the impact of Commission-approved energy

11        efficiency programs implemented during the base period; and (4) other known and

12        measurable changes. The Historical Test Year Period billing and usage data are

13        inputs into the jurisdictional and the class cost-of-service study ("CCOS")

14        allocations and form the basis for the billing determinants on which rates are

15        designed. An explanation for these adjustments is provided later in this section.

16               The adjustments to other operating revenues are also explained later in this

17        section of my testimony. I co-sponsor workpaper Adj. No. 1 to Schedule A-3,

18        which contains the revenue adjustments I describe in this testimony.

20        adjusted to account for known and measurable changes in the number of customers

21        or known energy and demand usage changes.
